claim_ceiling: Sources guide ARN representation only; they are not imported as proved Ignition claims.

sources.exact_claim: Learning can involve accretion, tuning, and restructuring rather than only adding facts.
sources.assumptions: Cognitive schema/network theory context; illustrative for representation, not clinical proof.
sources.usable_projection: IntegrationResponse distinguishes surface assimilation, local tuning/reconfiguration, and restructuring-like episodes.
sources.forbidden_upgrade: Do not diagnose a person or prove internal learning mechanism from behavior alone.
sources.evidence_class: primary/author source available via ERIC and paper scans
sources.citation: Rumelhart and Norman, Accretion, Tuning, and Restructuring: Three Modes of Learning; ERIC ED134902 / scanned paper.

sources.exact_claim: Accommodation of a new conception requires more than exposure; dissatisfaction and intelligibility/plausibility/fruitfulness conditions are discussed.
sources.assumptions: Science education conceptual change theory, not general psychological diagnosis.
sources.usable_projection: Perturbation may be rejected, context-gated, or locally integrated depending on conflicts and alternatives.
sources.forbidden_upgrade: Do not claim every change follows this model or infer private dissatisfaction from one output.
sources.citation: Posner, Strike, Hewson, Gertzog, Accommodation of a scientific conception: Toward a theory of conceptual change, Science Education 66, DOI 10.1002/sce.3730660207.

sources.exact_claim: Semantic processing can be modeled with activation spreading along associative links.
sources.assumptions: Semantic memory model; retrieval dynamics, not proof of durable integration.
sources.usable_projection: TemporalActivation and retrieval/repetition can be represented separately from judgment or action change.
sources.forbidden_upgrade: Do not equate activation or retrieval with learning or truth.
sources.citation: Collins and Loftus, A spreading-activation theory of semantic processing, Psychological Review 82(6), 1975, DOI 10.1037/0033-295X.82.6.407.

sources.exact_claim: A network of simple units can exhibit collective computational properties and attractor-like behavior in a mathematical/physical model.
sources.assumptions: Specific neural-network model class; not a direct cognitive or social proof.
sources.forbidden_upgrade: Do not infer human mental attractors or neural mechanisms from repository examples.
sources.citation: Hopfield, Neural networks and physical systems with emergent collective computational abilities, PNAS 79(8), DOI 10.1073/pnas.79.8.2554.

sources.exact_claim: Networks can have multiple layers and interlayer couplings with distinct representation choices.
sources.assumptions: Network-science modeling framework; layer definitions are model choices.
sources.forbidden_upgrade: Do not treat layer boundaries or multiplex representation as natural ontology.
sources.citation: Kivelä et al., Multilayer networks, Journal of Complex Networks 2(3):203-271, 2014; arXiv:1309.7233.

sources.exact_claim: Temporal ordering of contacts can change reachability; static aggregation can invent paths that are impossible in time.
sources.assumptions: Temporal network model with time-stamped edge activations.
sources.forbidden_upgrade: Do not infer temporal reachability from static adjacency alone.
sources.citation: Holme and Saramäki, Temporal Networks, Physics Reports 519(3):97-125, DOI 10.1016/j.physrep.2012.03.001; arXiv:1108.1780.

sources.exact_claim: Some interactions involve groups of three or more units and cannot be faithfully reduced to pairwise edges.
sources.assumptions: Higher-order network representations such as hypergraphs/simplicial complexes.
sources.forbidden_upgrade: Do not silently reduce higher-order relations to dyads.
sources.citation: Battiston et al., Networks beyond pairwise interactions: structure and dynamics, Physics Reports 874, 2020; arXiv:2006.01764.

sources.exact_claim: Behavior adoption can differ from simple information diffusion and may require social reinforcement from multiple neighbors.
sources.assumptions: Specific online social network experiment and health forum adoption behavior.
sources.usable_projection: Separate information exposure, social reinforcement, and action adoption evidence.
sources.forbidden_upgrade: Do not treat diffusion, exposure, or retrieval as behavior adoption or internal integration.
sources.citation: Centola, The spread of behavior in an online social network experiment, Science 329(5996), 2010, DOI 10.1126/science.1185231.
